kill_argument: The process account is now accurate, so the remaining case against the paper is about what it yields. Its clean reproductions are the cheap ones. Row 4 is reproduced, but on a balanced sample S1 is sd/sqrt(n), so matching its SEs identifies nothing. Table 4's N = 357 was seen at data prep, and once the SAS filter is used its coefficient follows. The estimate the literature argues about, row 3, is 'not reproduced as a whole'. Its points miss published precision for an unidentified reason, and its SE construction is unknown. H2 sets a half-magnitude bar that 5/95 winsorization rarely breaches, and the 0.85 it keeps reflects mostly capping eight large Pennsylvania declines, which says nothing about New Jersey. A referee could fairly say this is a careful ledger around a replication that Mamula had largely done. What I tried, and it held: `crew.py validate --strict` OK; every macro and table cell against claims and metrics; every paper-r1 response against the files; the gate, run and review times against log.jsonl; the source counts against sources.json; the replication claims against replication.json; the PDF's age against the sources; my decomposition of the H2 shrinkage from capped.csv.

findings.text: The title asks a causal question that the paper explicitly declines to answer. 'Did New Jersey's 1992 Minimum-Wage Increase Reduce Fast-Food Employment?' promises a verdict on the employment effect. But the text says the paper 'does not take a side in that dispute' (l.65). It draws 'no design-based inference' from any SE (abstract; Sec. 5, l.596-602). It maintains parallel trends without validating it (l.627-628). And it says 'nothing about which of those sources is right' (l.631-634). The reviewer role's paper check asks whether the title promises more than the result; this one does. The seed task's title is not a requirement in task.json. Resolve: Narrow the title to what was tested, for example 'Reproducing Card and Krueger (1994) from the Public Data: A Logged Replication with a Tail-Winsorization Check'.

It names the activity, not a verdict on the employment effect. task.json gives its title only as a seed label, so the change breaks no requirement.

findings.text: The paper's account of its own verification sequence is wrong, in a paper whose stated value is procedural. (a) main.tex l.337 says 'Before the design gate, a test script ran every estimator on a synthetic file'. log.jsonl shows the design gate approved at 2026-11-19T06:52:04Z. The econometrician brief (06:52:59Z) says the gate was already approved and asks for the code to be written. check-synthetic first ran at 07:01:20Z and again at 07:18:15Z. code-r1 is dated 07:06:34Z. So the code was written, tested and reviewed after the design gate. (b) plan.json task pi-design-gate reads 'Request and decide the design gate after design and code reviews' and is marked done, but the gate came before the code review. Neither the Deviations section nor the AI-use statement discloses this. Plan step 0d's binding condition (gate approved and code review clean before any analysis run) was met, so no estimate is affected. (c) l.110-112 says 'every analysis run was listed, with its metrics and decision rule, in a plan approved ... before any run; the code was reviewed before any run'. Four analysis-kind runs, pub-values, tab-replication, tab-h2 and fig-dfte-dist (runs/*/run.json kind=analysis, role figures-ra, 08:10Z), are not in the plan, and check-synthetic ran before the code review. The Presentation paragraph (l.668-675) discloses the table runs, which contradicts the introduction. Resolve: Rewrite l.337 to 'After the design gate and before any analysis run, ...'. Disclose in Deviations and disclosures that the design gate was approved before the code existed and before the code review, which departs from the plan's task description. Qualify l.110-112 as 'every planned analysis run' and 'before any analysis run', and point to the post-gate presentation runs.

findings.text: Parts of the H2 interpretation do not trace to claims. (a) l.535 'only one closure is capped, a Pennsylvania store' writes a result as a typed word, and no claim carries the closure's state (it comes from capped.csv). (b) l.539-543: 'Winsorization therefore mostly reshapes the changes of large stores at the bottom of the distribution, the size class for which Ropponen reports negative effects.' No logged metric splits the shrinkage. My own arithmetic on the logged runs/h2-winsor/capped.csv (no new estimation) splits the -0.41 change in the DiD as follows: PA low tail -0.61 (8 stores, mean FTE1 45.7), NJ low +0.19, NJ high -0.28, PA high +0.29. The net shrinkage comes from capping declines at eight large control-state stores, which says nothing about Ropponen's heterogeneity of New Jersey treatment effects, so placing the two side by side misleads. (c) l.549-551 says the estimate 'is not produced by the few stores beyond the 5th and 95th percentiles'. Winsorization caps those stores and does not remove them, so what it shows concerns the part of their changes beyond the cutoffs. Resolve: Use \HTwoCappedLowClosed. Drop the Ropponen size-class sentence, or state, from a logged metric, that the shrinkage comes mainly from capping eight large Pennsylvania low-tail stores (which fits limitation T7). Reword (c) to 'not produced by the parts of the changes beyond the cutoffs'.
findings.response: Writer: '(in Pennsylvania)' removed; the 'mainly the Pennsylvania low tail' attribution dropped and replaced by 'no logged run splits the narrowing by state and tail, so we do not attribute it'; Ropponen sentence now rests only on capped changes not being effect estimates and coming from both states.
findings.ruling: Partly fixed. (a) The count is now \HTwoCappedLowClosed. (c) l.557-560 now say winsorization caps rather than removes. The Ropponen juxtaposition is replaced by the correct statement that the narrowing says nothing about New Jersey heterogeneity. Two traceability gaps remain. First, l.532 still types '(in Pennsylvania)' for the capped closure; no claim carries it, and the fact comes only from capped.csv via runs/NOTES.md l.259. Second, l.549-551 says the shrinkage 'comes mainly from capping the declines of the Pennsylvania stores in the low tail', and the next words point to Table 2 for 'the capped counts by state and tail'. Those counts (NJ 12/16, PA 8/4) cannot show that. My arithmetic on the logged capped.csv (no estimation) confirms the statement is true: PA low -0.608, NJ high -0.279, NJ low +0.185, PA high +0.292, net -0.4105 = did_w - did_u. But the paper's reader cannot check it, and the paper rests its value on traceability. Severity stays minor.

findings.text: Two wordings conflict with numbers elsewhere in the paper. (a) l.578 'The 71 New Jersey stores that already paid $5.00 or more' sits against l.203-204, which gives 73 such stores. The 71 are the stores with wave-1 FTE (claim placebo-hiwage-n), and the paper does not explain the difference. (b) The Conclusion (l.690) says the row-3 standard errors 'are not reproduced'. That departs from the pre-fixed wording 'point reproduced; SE construction not identified' and from Table 1, where the PA and DiD SEs are within tolerance and only the NJ SE misses. Resolve: Write 'the 71 of these 73 stores with first-wave employment data'. Use the pre-fixed SE wording in the Conclusion.
